I changed the upstream CONNECT authority so an IPv6 literal target is now bracketed, for example `[::1]:443` instead of `::1:443`. I didn't add a test, run the test suite, or run the code.

The fix is in `HttpUpstreamProxy.start_handshake` in `mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/_upstream_proxy.py`. After the host is IDNA-encoded, any host containing `:` is wrapped in `[...]` before the port is appended. The bracketed authority is also what goes into the optional `Host` header and the request's `authority` field, so both stay consistent.

I didn't look closely at the existing CONNECT tests in `test/mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/test_http.py`, so I don't know how easily an IPv6 case would fit there.
